summary: Rate-tag shadowing causes unexpected invoice credit reclassification for BrightFlow Analytics
description: Issue summary: Customer BrightFlow Analytics reports that their March invoice shows a reclassified credit line ("eco-sustainability-surcharge-credit") and a corresponding unexpected surcharge line. Impact: invoice total higher than expected by $12,540; customer is requesting explanation and provisional credit while we investigate. Environment: prod (us-west-2). Account: brightflow-acct-9812. Invoice: INV-2026-03-09-BFA. Observed behavior: console estimate for March usage matched previous cycles but finalized invoice contains a one-off credit reclassification and a matching surcharge that net to a partial charge. Customer noticed this after merge of two billing tags during an org split last week.
steps_to_reproduce: Customer performed org merge and then executed a pricing-tag migration on 2026-03-04
Billing service evaluated postbacks for usage bucket brightflow-9812 between 2026-03-01 and 2026-03-08
Console estimate (daily) showed expected buffer credits and sustainability discounts; final invoice has reclassified credit + extra surcharge line
Attempt to reproduce locally using replay tool with postback id 8f3b2c produced different tag precedence output
logs: 2026-03-05T02:14:22Z billing-eval INFO postback_id=8f3b2c priced_rate_tags=[org:enterprise, legacy:eco-flag] final_rate=standard
2026-03-09T04:12:03Z pricing-service ERROR tag_precedence_conflict detected: sourceA=pricing-override sourceB=org-default married=true
comments: 2026-03-10 08:12 - Aisha Patel (Support): Opened ticket after customer email; requested invoice PDF and postback IDs. Asked finance for provisional credit hold.
2026-03-10 09:05 - Marco Li (Billing Eng): Acknowledged, started replay of postbacks for account brightflow-9812 and scoped to pricing-service logs. Noted tag merge event on 2026-03-04.
2026-03-10 11:23 - BrightFlow (Customer, Elena Marques): Provided invoice PDF and confirmed org-split timeline; asked for provisional credit while engineers validate.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: pricing tag precedence bug where transient tag from org-split (legacy:eco-flag) shadowed hourly-buffer credits and caused reclassification
Reproducer: replaying postback stream with standard precedence rules yields expected hourly-buffer credit; replay with live precedence dataset from 2026-03-04 yields shadowed mapping

Pricing-service change on 2026-03-04 (PR #4121) introduced a merge path that reads both 'org-tags' and 'legacy-pricing-tags' and resolves conflicts by last-write; this can result in eco-flag taking precedence over buffer-tag in merged metadata
Reconciler applied a second billing rule (sustainability surcharge) because the mapping reported rate_tag=eco-flag and also applied an ad-hoc surcharge rule for that tag
No evidence of double-charging for identical tokens; issue is credit reclassification and subsequent surcharge rule application, netting a charge
resolution: Workaround applied: provisional credit of $12,540 issued to BrightFlow (finance ticket FIN-2026-183). Short-term fix: rollback PR #4121 in staging and gated guard added to pricing-service to prefer 'hourly-buffer' tag for accounts with active reserved-capacity flags. Long-term fix: implement deterministic tag-precedence policy and add an opt-out flag for legacy eco-tag migration flows. Follow-up: schedule deployment of deterministic precedence policy and add e2e test that replays org-split postbacks (owner: Marco Li, ETA 2026-03-17). Customer notified of provisional credit and ETA for permanent fix.

Customer agreed to provisional credit while we confirm permanent remediation
Customer asked for a short runbook to avoid tag merges during active billing cycles
